title: Kernel Preference Cache (PrefCache) + Bayesian Autotuner for mixed-length workloads
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Background:
We observe that optimal kernels vary deterministically with hardware family, model architecture, and sequence-length distribution, but also drift with batch shape and temperature/decoding modes. Existing offline heuristics (static tables) and heavy-weight per-request probes are either stale or too costly.

Proposal summary:
Introduce a lightweight Kernel Preference Cache (PrefCache) keyed by model-version + arch + seqlen-bucket + decode-mode that stores a ranked list of candidate kernels with recent empirical cost/latency estimates and confidence. Complement PrefCache with a Bayesian Autotuner: a low-traffic exploration policy using Thompson-sampling-like bandit trials to update PrefCache scores online, while maintaining a safety policy that falls back to a conservative kernel for latency/regression protection.

Goals:
- Reduce median and tail latency for mixed-length traffic by selecting near-optimal kernels per-request without per-request micro-benchmarks.
- Keep exploration budget low (<1% of requests in steady state) and avoid regressions (p95 within 10% of baseline).
- Provide observability and rollback for any kernel-choice changes.

Design notes and heuristics:
- Keys & Buckets: seqlen-buckets determined by percentiles (0-8,9-32,33-128,129-512,>512) derived from rolling 7-day traces per model; architecture tag uses family+smaller hw fingerprint (e.g., A100-40GB, H100-80GB).
- PrefCache entry: ranked candidates with score "mean latency" and "uncertainty" (tau). Keep TTL of 12 hours; evict cold entries after 30 days.
- Exploration: for cold or uncertain entries, route 0.5-2% of requests to candidate kernels chosen by Bayesian sampling. Use stratified sampling across seqlen buckets to ensure coverage.
- Safety policy: each sampled request runs with a latency SLO guardrail; if candidate kernel exceeds SLO by X ms or triggers OOM/other fatal, mark candidate as failed and disable for that key for 1h. Global circuit breaker prevents rollout of any kernel causing >0.5% error increase cluster-wide over a 5m window.
- Cost model: in addition to latency, track tokens/sec and GPU utilization; computed score is a weighted utility = latency_penalty + alpha*cost_delta. alpha tunable per-customer (Dedicated/Private higher weight).
- Warmstart: initialize PrefCache using offline microbench matrix (existing kernel profiler outputs) and a small synthetic probe burst on rollout.

Experiment plan:
1) Simulation: run replay of 14 days of production traces through an offline PrefCache simulator to estimate potential wins and failure modes. Metrics: latency p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, cost-per-token delta.
2) Canary: enable exploration on 1% traffic for non-critical model-version in us-west-2. Compare candidate wins. 48-hour min run.
3) Gradual rollout: move to 10% then 30% with smoke checks and automatic rollback on regressions.

Acceptance criteria:
- Simulator shows >=6% reduction in average latency for heterogeneous workloads or >=2% reduction in cost-per-token without >10% p95 regression in worst-case model groups.
- Canary: no regressions in p95 beyond threshold; no increase in OOMs or fatal errors; PrefCache update rate stabilizes.

Monitoring & observability:
- New telemetry streams: per-prefcache-key stats (requests, wins, losses, mean latency, uncertainty), exploration fraction, candidate-failure events.
- Dashboards: PrefCache health, per-model bucket top-k kernels, canary watchdog.
- Alerts: p95 regression, candidate-failure-rate spike, global circuit breaker trip.

Rollout and rollout controls:
- Feature flag: runtime.prefcache.autotune with knobs for exploration_fraction, alpha, seqlen-buckets override.
- Rollout states: off -> sim-only -> canary -> gradual -> active. Each state requires manual approval except automated rollback triggers.

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: noisy short-lived seqlen spikes cause oscillation. Mitigation: exponential decay + min-sample threshold for cache updates.
- Risk: GPU kernel selection causing memory fragmentation/OOM. Mitigation: fail-fast detection and candidate blacklisting + global breaker.

Dependencies:
- requires runtime telemetry extension (ENG-47290) to emit per-kernel micrometrics (latency slices, mem peaks).
- needs seqlen percentile job in metrics pipeline (PM/infra).
- coordinate with Dedicated team for alpha parameter tuning on reserved GPU pools.

Links to artifacts and PRs:
- Design doc (Confluence): https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/RUNTIME/pages/PrefCache+Design+Draft
- Offline simulator repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/prefcache-sim (WIP)
- Draft PR (runtime): https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1182
- Bench dashboard (canary): https://grafana.redwood.cloud/d/prefcache/canary-run

Notes on uniqueness vs prior work:
This approach departs from heavier, per-request probing autotuners in existing tickets by caching and decoupling exploration from every request. The Bayesian sampling prioritizes informative trials and quantifies uncertainty explicitly which should reduce wasted probes for stable key spaces. It also formalizes a safety-first circuit to prevent regressions during live tuning.
